Set route average speed

Source: R/set_route_speed.R
set_route_speed.Rd

Sets the average speed of the trips of each specified route_id, or of a segment of them, by changing the arrival_time and departure_time columns in stop_times.

Usage

set_route_speed(
  gtfs,
  route_id,
  speed,
  unit = "km/h",
  first_stop = NULL,
  last_stop = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  by_reference = FALSE
)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs().

route_id

A character vector including the route_ids to have the average speed of their trips set.

speed

A numeric representing the speed to be set. Its length must either equal 1, in which case the value is recycled for all route_ids, or equal route_id's length. Must be positive and finite.

unit

A string representing the unit in which the speed is given. One of "km/h" (the default), "m/s" or "mph" (miles per hour).

first_stop

A string. The stop_id where the segment whose speed is set starts. If NULL (the default), the segment starts at each trip's first stop.

last_stop

A string. The stop_id where the segment ends. If NULL (the default), the segment ends at each trip's last stop.

from

A string, in the "HH:MM:SS" format. Only trips that depart from the segment's first stop at or after from are changed. If NULL (the default), there is no lower limit.

to

A string, in the "HH:MM:SS" format. Only trips that depart from the segment's first stop at or before to are changed. If NULL (the default), there is no upper limit.

by_reference

Whether to update stop_times' data.table by reference. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

If by_reference is set to FALSE, returns a GTFS object with the time columns of its stop_times adjusted. Else, returns a GTFS object invisibly (note that in this case the original GTFS object is altered).

Details

Every trip of each route, as listed in trips, gets the route's speed, as in set_trip_speed(), whose details also apply here: the duration of each trip's segment (by default, the whole trip) is set to its length divided by speed, the times at stops inside the segment are set to "", and from and to restrict the changes to the trips that depart from the segment's first stop within the time of day. Warnings about trips that can't be changed refer to their trip_ids. Trips without stop_times entries are ignored.

See also

set_trip_speed(), get_trip_speed(), get_route_speed()

Examples

library(dplyr)

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")
gtfs <- read_gtfs(data_path)

route_trips <- gtfs$trips |>
  filter(route_id == "CPTM L07") |>
  pull(trip_id)
get_trip_speed(gtfs, route_trips)
#> Key: <trip_id>
#>    route_id    trip_id    speed
#>      <char>     <char>    <num>
#> 1: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0 26.73002
#> 2: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-1 26.73002

new_speed_gtfs <- set_route_speed(gtfs, route_id = "CPTM L07", speed = 50)
get_trip_speed(new_speed_gtfs, route_trips)
#> Key: <trip_id>
#>    route_id    trip_id    speed
#>      <char>     <char>    <num>
#> 1: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-0 50.00388
#> 2: CPTM L07 CPTM L07-1 50.00388

# set the speed only of the trips that depart within a time of day
poa_path <- system.file("extdata/poa_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")
poa_gtfs <- read_gtfs(poa_path)

poa_new_speed <- set_route_speed(
  poa_gtfs,
  route_id = "T2",
  speed = 25,
  from = "07:00:00",
  to = "09:00:00"
)

# the arrival at the last stop of a trip that departs at 07:02 changes
poa_gtfs$stop_times |>
  filter(trip_id == "T2-1@1#702") |>
  slice_tail(n = 1)
#>       trip_id arrival_time departure_time stop_id stop_sequence
#>        <char>       <char>         <char>  <char>         <int>
#> 1: T2-1@1#702     08:03:00       08:03:00    1456            62

poa_new_speed$stop_times |>
  filter(trip_id == "T2-1@1#702") |>
  slice_tail(n = 1)
#> Index: <trip_id>
#>       trip_id arrival_time departure_time stop_id stop_sequence
#>        <char>       <char>         <char>  <char>         <int>
#> 1: T2-1@1#702     07:41:39       07:41:39    1456            62
